literal: With a pleased heart, the Goddess of Wealth will dwell in the home of him who, with a pleased face, cherishes a good guest.
translation: The Goddess of Wealth will joyfully make her home with the one who welcomes worthy guests with a cheerful face.
modern: முகமலர்ச்சியோடு நல்ல விருந்தினரை வரவேற்று உபசரிப்பவனுடைய வீட்டில், திருமகள் தன் மனம் மகிழ்ந்து வாழ்வாள்.
explanation: This couplet highlights the immense reward of hospitality by drawing a beautiful parallel between the host and the goddess of wealth. The words 'அகன்' (heart) and 'முகன்' (face) are variants of 'அகம்' and 'முகம்'. When a host welcomes a guest with a cheerful face ('முகன் அமர்ந்து'), the goddess of wealth ('செய்யாள்') is so pleased that she resides in that home with a joyful heart ('அகன் அமர்ந்து'). The poet shows that outward warmth to guests invites divine, lasting prosperity into one's home.
